problems.title: Shelf Signatures
problems.statement: A bookshop labels each shelf with a word. Two labels are shelf-mates when one can be rearranged into the other using every letter exactly once. Group all labels into maximal sets of shelf-mates (an identical label that appears twice counts as two members of its set). Report how many sets exist and how many members the largest set has.
problems.inputFormat: Line 1: n. Then n lines, each holding one lowercase word.
problems.outputFormat: Two integers separated by a space: the number of sets, then the size of the largest set.
constraints: Each word has 1 to 20 lowercase letters a-z
The whole input is at most 64 KiB

problems.title: Wildcard Lexicon
problems.statement: A crossword helper stores n words. Each query is a pattern of the same length as the word wanted, where a '.' stands for exactly one unknown letter and any other character must match exactly. For every pattern answer whether at least one stored word fits it completely (same length, every position compatible).
problems.inputFormat: Line 1: n and q. Then n lines, one lowercase word each. Then q lines, one pattern each (lowercase letters and '.').
problems.outputFormat: q tokens YES or NO separated by single spaces on one line.
constraints: Words and patterns have 1 to 20 characters
Words contain only lowercase letters; patterns also allow '.'

problems.statement: A cipher machine holds n keys, each a non-negative integer. Mixing two different keys (two different positions in the list) produces the bitwise XOR of their values. Find the largest value any mixture can produce. Two keys with the same value may be mixed, which yields 0.
problems.inputFormat: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.
problems.outputFormat: One integer: the maximum XOR over all pairs of distinct positions.
